title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttentionV2 + fused rope/rotary ops, KV batching & scheduler tweaks
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: improve single-request latency and steady-state throughput for long-context workloads by upgrading the attention kernels and reducing KV-cache overhead. This PR replaces the ad-hoc FlashAttention wrapper with a V2-compatible kernel, folds fused rotary/rope computation into the attention kernel where beneficial, and tightens KV-batching and scheduler heuristics to reduce tail latency under mixed workloads.

Summary of changes: 1) Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels and update our kernel-selection logic to prefer FA2 for supported CUDA/SM archs; 2) Add fused rotary/rope code paths inside the kernel and a safe fallback for models that require explicit rotary/rope preprocessing; 3) Introduce a KV-batching window parameter + continuous-batching fast-path to prioritize short-latency requests; 4) Scheduler tweaks: introduce per-model latency weight and backpressure signal to avoid queue head-of-line blocking; 5) Updated build scripts to compile FA2 kernels with our internal flags and CI GPU matrix.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel integration and unit-tests - [x] Benchmarks (micro and end-to-end) - [x] CI GPU matrix passing - [x] Canary rollout plan drafted - [x] Documentation updates for kernel selection flags

Testing & results: Microbenchmarks show median token latency improvement of 6-12% and 99th percentile improvements of 10-18% on A100/40GB for sequence lengths 2k-8k. End-to-end e2e benchmark (concurrent chat workload) shows 8% cost reduction due to better batching and 12% improvement in p99 latency after enabling the KV-batching fast-path. We observed no quality regressions on our eval sets (generation perplexity and deterministic sampling checks).

Rollout plan: staged canary across Dedicated pools: start with canary=5% with FA2 enabled + fused-rotary=true, monitor per-token latency, p99, and error rates for 48h, then increase to 25% and finally full. Auto-fallback to previous kernel is enabled on error or latency regressions.

Notes: The fused rotary/rope code path is enabled behind a runtime flag to allow quick rollback. We added a model-compatibility table for FA2 support and updated the model registry entries with recommended flags.

References: ENG-4123 (performance spike investigation), SUP-1182 (support case for degraded latency on long context), prior PRs: pr-20542, pr-45901, pr-51234 for historical kernel work.
